extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), and patent examiners handling appeals before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing and filing appeal briefs and related submissions (amendments, affidavits/evidence) in USPTO patent appeals, including timing, required content headings, appendix requirements, and procedures for amendments/evidence after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Filing Appeal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant has 2 months from the date of the notice of appeal to file an appeal brief and pay the appeal brief fee under 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2) (37 CFR 41.37(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2-month period is measured from the Office date of receipt of the notice of appeal (not a Certificate of Mailing). If notice is filed under 37 CFR 1.10 using USPS Express Mail 'post office to addressee', the date of deposit is the receipt date. The rule does not permit using the time for reply to the last Office action even if that time is later; filing a notice of appeal tolls the reply period. Time may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a), or under 1.136(b) for extraordinary circumstances if (a) is not available; additional time in excess of 5 months will not be granted unless extraordinary circumstances. Extensions are added to the calendar day of the original period. If unable to file in time, appellant may petition (with fee) to the Technology Center under 37 CFR 1.136(a); if that is exhausted, seek 1.136(b). Examples provided regarding RCEs and petitions clarify when extensions/petitions are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal Brief Fee and Copy Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any appeal brief must be accompanied by the appeal brief fee under 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2). Only one copy of the appeal brief is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The brief and every document relating to an appeal should indicate the Technology Center number and the application or reexamination control number. Briefs filed (or having a certificate of mailing) prior to September 13, 2004 may comply with earlier rules (37 CFR 1.192) but briefs filed on/after that date must comply with 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of Noncompliant Brief or Failure To Timely File
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief does not comply with 37 CFR 41.37(c), appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given time to file an amended brief; failure to timely file a compliant amended brief will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the brief and required fee within the permissible time ordinarily results in dismissal (with limited exceptions like interference declarations). If any claims stand allowed, dismissal does not abandon the application but it is returned to the examiner for action on allowed claims; if no allowed claims, application is abandoned as of the date the brief was due. In reexamination proceedings, failure to file can result in issuance of the certificate under 37 CFR 1.570 or 1.997. When notified of non-compliance, appellant may file a petition under 37 CFR 41.3, but filing a petition does not toll the time to reply to the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: BPAI Determination of Brief Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (BPAI) has sole responsibility for determining whether appeal briefs comply with 37 CFR 41.37 and will complete that determination (normally within ~1 month) before forwarding the brief to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the BPAI finds the brief compliant or with only minor informalities, it will accept and forward it. If non-compliant, BPAI will notify appellant to file a corrected brief within a set time or the appeal may be dismissed. Once accepted by BPAI, the brief will not later be held defective by the Patent Appeal Center or the examiner. Examiners should not use prior form PTOL-462; BPAI will correspond directly with appellant on non-compliant issues. Examiners still retain jurisdiction to consider the appeal and prepare examiner's answers; BPAI's role is limited to notifying non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness to Every Ground of Rejection Presented
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant's brief must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner that the appellant presents for review in the appeal; any ground not addressed will be summarily sustained by the Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oral argument cannot remedy a deficiency of the brief. The brief must set forth the authorities and arguments relied upon and fully state appellant's position with respect to each ground so the Board need not search the record. Merely filing a paper labeled 'brief' is insufficient without the required authorities/arguments and structure under 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Real Party in Interest (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must include a statement identifying by name the real party in interest, even if the party named in the caption is the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification allows Board members to avoid conflicts of interest. When assigned to a subsidiary, the real party may include assignee and parent corporation(s). Failure to name the real party under this heading will prompt notification of defect and a time period to amend; failure to timely correct can result in dismissal. Example wording: 'The real party in interest is XXXX corporation, the assignee of record, which is a subsidiary of a joint venture between YYYY corporation and ZZZZ corporation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Appeals and Interferences (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must identify all prior and pending appeals, judicial proceedings, or interferences known to appellant that may be related to or affect the Board's decision, identified by application/patent/appeal/interference number if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement includes commonly owned applications with common subject matter or claims to common priority. Copies of any decisions rendered in identified proceedings must be included in the related proceedings appendix. If none, state 'none'. If appellant does not identify any items, it will be presumed there are none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of Claims (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must state the status of all claims in the application or patent under reexamination (for each claim, whether cancelled, allowed/confirmed, rejected, withdrawn, objected to, etc.) and identify each claim on appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This avoids confusion about which claims are on appeal and their precise wording, especially if appellant sought to amend claims after final rejection. Inclusion allows examiner and Board to resolve disagreements about claim status before decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of Amendments (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must state the status of any amendment filed subsequent to final rejection (whether acted on by the examiner and whether entered or denied entry), as understood by appellant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellants are encouraged to check PAIR for the status of amendments or affidavits filed after final rejection or after filing the notice of appeal. This clarifies post-final amendments and helps resolve disagreements prior to Board consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of Claimed Subject Matter (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each independent claim involved in the appeal, referring to the specification by page and line number and to drawings by reference characters; for each independent and separately argued dependent claim, identify every means-plus-function/step-plus-function and corresponding structure/material/acts in the specification by page and line and drawing references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to page and line numbers helps the Board quickly find the described matter. Failure to provide the required summary will prompt notification of defect and a time period to amend. For means/step-plus-function claims (35 U.S.C. 112, sixth paragraph), appellant must identify corresponding structure in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds of Rejection To Be Reviewed (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise statement of each ground of rejection presented for review (e.g., 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable under 35 U.S.C. 103 over Smith in view of Jones').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements must be specific as to statutory basis and references; general statements like 'Whether claims 1 and 2 are unpatentable' do not comply. The statement must not include argument — arguments belong in the Argument section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant's contentions with respect to each ground of rejection presented and the basis for those contentions, including citations of authorities, statutes, and parts of the record relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A mere recitation of what a claim recites is not an argument. Any arguments/authorities not included in the brief or reply brief filed pursuant to § 41.41 will be refused consideration by the Board unless good cause is shown. Arguments first made at oral hearing are normally not considered. Supplemental papers are allowed if new authority becomes available after filing (e.g., a newly published court decision). Each ground must be treated under a separate heading; claims may be argued separately or grouped (but grouping may waive separate consideration). Use subheadings identifying claims when arguing multiple claims; the Board may decide grouped claims based on a single selected claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Appendix (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The copy should be a clean copy without markings (except in reissue applications or specific reexamination rules), double-spaced, and the appendix should start on a new page. See MPEP §1454 for reissue claim presentation and 37 CFR 1.530(d)/(f) for reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Appendix (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to 37 CFR 1.130–1.132 or any other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by appellant in the appeal, along with a statement where in the record that evidence was entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted in the brief. The appendix should start on a new page. If there is no evidence relied upon by appellant, include an evidence appendix labeled 'none'. See 37 CFR 41.33 and MPEP §2274 for treatment of evidence submitted after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related Proceedings Appendix (37 CFR 41.37(c)(1)(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing copies of decisions rendered by a court or the Board in any proceeding identified under the 'related appeals and interferences' section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appendix should start on a new page. If no such decisions are being submitted, include a related proceedings appendix labeled 'none'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro Se Exception for Brief Content Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application is prosecuted pro se (no attorney/agent of record) and the brief was neither prepared nor signed by a registered practitioner, the brief will be accepted if it substantially complies with items (i)–(iv) and (vii)–(x) of 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, strict inclusion of all items (i)–(x) is relaxed for bona fide pro se appellants, but key items remain required. If relying on references, pro se appellants are still expected to provide copies in the evidence appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Inclusion of New or Non-Admitted Amendments/Evidence in Brief (37 CFR 41.37(c)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief may not include any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any new amendment/evidence must be submitted and considered under the appropriate rules for amendments/evidence after appeal (see 37 CFR 41.33 and related sections). Inclusion of unadmitted evidence in the brief is prohibited and may render the brief non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested Format and Example Content Order for an Appeal Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An example brief format: (A) Identification page; (B) Table of Contents; (C) Real party in interest; (D) Related appeals and interferences; (E) Status of claims; (F) Status of amendments; (G) Summary of claimed subject matter; (H) Grounds of rejection to be reviewed on appeal; (I) Argument; (J) Claims appendix; (K) Evidence appendix; (L) Related proceedings appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item should start on a separate page. The rule specifies these items as the minimum and does not prohibit inclusion of additional materials (list of references, table of cases, etc.). A brief is compliant if it includes items (i)–(x) in the order set forth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments Filed After Notice of Appeal But Before Filing Brief (37 CFR 41.33(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after notice of appeal but prior to filing a brief may be admitted as provided in 37 CFR 1.116; specifically, such amendments may be admitted to cancel claims, to comply with form requirements set in a previous action, to present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal, or to amend specification/claims upon a showing of good and sufficient reasons why necessary and not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry of a new amendment is not a matter of right and is governed by 37 CFR 41.33 (not 1.116). If the examiner denies entry, use PTOL-303 to notify applicant of non-entry and reasons. Examiners must respond to all amendments filed after appeal and prior to termination; if an amendment clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter and allow it. Otherwise, entry is limited to the situations permitted by the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments Filed On or After Filing Brief (37 CFR 41.33(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed on or after the filing date of the brief may be admitted only to cancel claims (without affecting scope of other pending claims) or to rewrite dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form includes (A) rewriting a dependent claim into independent form by adding parent claim limitations, and (B) rewriting an independent claim to incorporate subject matter of a dependent claim, canceling the dependent claim, and adjusting dependencies of other claims accordingly. If examiner denies entry of such an amendment after the brief, use PTOL-304 to notify applicant of non-entry and reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of Affidavits or Other Evidence Filed After Notice of Appeal But Before Filing Brief (37 CFR 41.33(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or other evidence submitted after notice of appeal but prior to filing a brief may be admitted if the examiner determines the evidence overcomes all rejections under appeal and there is a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner denies entry, PTOL-303 should be used to notify applicant of non-entry and the reason. This standard applies to affidavits/declarations/exhibits submitted in that window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of Affidavits or Other Evidence Filed On or After Filing Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: All other affidavits or evidence filed after the date of filing a brief will not be admitted except as permitted by specific provisions (e.g., §§ 41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i), 41.50(b)(1) and 41.50(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence filed on/after the brief is subject to narrow exceptions in the rules; reference to 37 CFR 41.33 and MPEP sections for precise permitted circumstances (generally not admitted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's Responsibilities Regarding Post-Appeal Amendments and Advisory Actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must respond to all amendments filed after appeal and prior to termination. If an advisory action indicates an amendment would be entered, the examiner must state how individual rejections would be impacted, except where the amendment merely cancels claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner determines an amendment places the application clearly in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the amendment and allow the application. For denials of entry, examiners should use PTOL-303 (before filing brief) or PTOL-304 (after filing brief) to notify the applicant and state reasons for non-entry. Entry of amendment on appeal is governed by 37 CFR 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies Following Abandonment or Dismissal for Failure To File Brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If application becomes abandoned for failure to file a brief, applicant may petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137. If appeal is dismissed but application not abandoned because at least one claim is allowed, applicant may petition to reinstate the claims and the appeal, subject to a showing equivalent to a petition to revive under 37 CFR 1.137.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reinstate an appeal, in addition to the petition and fee, appellant must file either (A) an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 accompanied by a reply submission and fee if appropriate, or (B) an appeal brief and the appeal brief fee. A proper brief and fee must be filed before the petition will be considered on its merits. Where dismissal is believed in error, a petition pointing out the error may suffice.
